calls.title: Calls (STUN and TURN)
calls.loadError: Could not load the call settings.
calls.intro: Messages and call signaling always go through this server. Only the audio and video between participants needs STUN or TURN, and only when two people cannot reach each other directly: on the same network calls just work, across routers and NAT they need this.
calls.statusOn: The built-in STUN/TURN server is running on port {port}.
calls.statusFailed: The built-in server could not start
calls.statusDetail: Active relays: {relays}. Relays since start: {total}. Data relayed: {data}.
calls.warn_noExternalIp: No public address is known. Set the external IP below, otherwise people outside your network cannot use the relay.
calls.warn_privatePeers: Relaying to private addresses is on, so the relay can reach machines inside your network. Turn it off unless you need it.
calls.externalIpHint: The public IPv4 address of this machine as the internet sees it. Detect asks a public STUN server once, only when you press the button.
calls.tcp: Also accept TCP connections (helps behind strict firewalls)
calls.portHint: The default 3478 is the standard STUN/TURN port.
calls.relayRangeHint: Each relayed call stream uses one port from this range. Keep at least a few dozen.
calls.advertisedHostHint: Leave empty to use the external IP, then the public host, then the address the browser used.
calls.privatePeersHint: Only needed when the TURN server and the people using it share one private network.
calls.forwardBody: When this machine is behind a router, forward UDP and TCP {port} and UDP {lo}-{hi} to it. setup-turn.bat (Windows) or setup-turn.sh (Linux) opens the firewall on this machine for you.
calls.testNote: This tests the server from this machine. To test from the internet, join a call from a phone on mobile data.
calls.externalHint: Optional. Servers you run elsewhere or rent. Signed-in users receive them together with the built-in one.
calls.lanHint: Leave empty for automatic: people on the same LAN or VPN (Radmin, ZeroTier, SoftEther, Hamachi) already connect directly. List subnets here only to make calls settle faster when users have extra adapters (Docker, WSL, virtual machines). One IPv4 CIDR per line.
calls.lanExamples: Examples: 192.168.1.0/24 (home LAN), 26.0.0.0/8 (Radmin VPN), 25.0.0.0/8 (Hamachi), 10.147.17.0/24 (ZeroTier network). Public, STUN and TURN paths are never blocked.
calls.howBody:
1. Direct: the two people try every address they have (LAN, VPN, public) at once and use the fastest that works. No server is involved in the audio, nothing leaves your network.
2. STUN: an external or built-in STUN server only tells a person their public address. It carries no audio. Needed when people are behind different routers.
3. TURN: relays the audio when no direct path works (strict firewalls, mobile data). Uses server bandwidth. Enable the built-in one above, or add an external TURN with user name and password below.
4. A call that drops is retried automatically, and falls back to the next option. Hover the colored dot on a person's tile to see which path is in use.
External entries look like stun:stun.example.com:3478 or turn:turn.example.com:3478 (turns: for TLS). Several addresses of one server go in one row, comma separated.
calls.detectFailed: Could not reach a public STUN server.

security.title: Security Center
security.intro: Keeps bots and floods away from sign-in and the rest of the server. Captcha settings, automatic bans, manual IP bans and subscribed blocklists all live here. Everything is checked on this server; nothing is sent to a third party.
security.underAttackOn: Under attack mode is ON until {until}
security.underAttackHint: While on, every sign-in and sign-up needs a captcha, whatever the captcha settings say. It switches on by itself after a burst of automatic bans (see Protection).
security.sinceStart: Since the server started: {issued} captchas shown, {solved} solved, {failed} failed.
security.captchaIntro: A captcha is a picture the visitor has to read before signing in or signing up. It is drawn on this server, so nothing leaves your network.
security.captchaAfterHint: Counted per network address, separately for sign-in and sign-up. A successful sign-in resets the sign-in count.
security.excludeAmbiguous: Leave out look-alike characters (0 O 1 I)
security.wordCountHint: Several words are harder for bots but slower for people.
security.customWordsHint: One word per line, 3 to 14 characters. Accents are removed (Ház is shown and accepted as HAZ). At least 10 are needed when you use only your own list.
security.previewHint: Press the button to see a sample with the settings above, before saving.
security.protectionIntro: These limits act on one network address at a time. Allowlisted addresses are never banned. A shared address (an office, a school) counts as one visitor, so keep the limits generous.
security.protModeHint: Manual bans and blocklists always apply, whatever this is set to.
security.floodHint: Only dynamic requests from visitors who are not signed in count; script, style, image and upload files, signed-in users and private addresses never do.
security.banLengthHint: Doubles for every earlier automatic ban of the same address within 24 hours (up to 7 days).
security.scannersHint: Hits on paths like /wp-login.php or /.env inside the violation window above.
security.strikesHint: Counts visitors who keep hitting the built-in rate limits while not signed in.
security.honeypot: Bot traps on the sign-in and sign-up forms
security.honeypotHint: A hidden field and a speed check that people never trigger but simple bots do.
security.autoAttackHint: Many different addresses getting banned at once usually means a spread-out attack.
security.allowlistHint: One address, range (1.2.3.4-1.2.3.9) or network (10.0.0.0/8) per line. These are never banned or limited. 127.0.0.1 and ::1 are there so the machine itself can always get in. Behind a reverse proxy, set trustProxy in config.json, or every visitor looks like the proxy.
security.bansIntro: Banned addresses get "Access denied" on every request, including live connections. Bans can last forever or expire.
security.banHint: A single address, a range (1.2.3.4-1.2.3.9) or a network (10.0.0.0/8). IPv6 works too. You cannot ban your own address.
security.clearAutoConfirm: Remove all automatic bans? Addresses that are still misbehaving will be banned again.
security.listsIntro: A blocklist is a public list of known bad addresses that this server downloads and keeps up to date. Only https addresses are accepted, and only the list itself is fetched. If an update fails, the previous copy stays in force.
security.listsHint: One address or network per line; lines starting with # or ; are comments. Lists are limited to 50,000 entries. Allowlisted addresses are never blocked by a list.
security.firstFetchFailed: Added, but the first download failed: {error}
security.lookupIntro: Check what this server knows about an address: whether it is blocked, by which ban or list, and what it did recently.
security.lkCaptchaYes: captcha is required for this address now
security.clearEventsConfirm: Delete the whole security event log?

passport.title: Your Passport
passport.intro: Your Passport is your identity. It belongs to you, not to this server. Export it to a file and keep that file safe: with it you can sign in or recover your account on this or any other MeshCrowd server.
passport.passphraseTooShort: The passphrase must be at least {min} characters.
passport.neverExported: You have not exported a Passport file yet. Without one you cannot recover this account if you forget your password.
passport.noSeedOnDevice: This device does not hold your Passport key. Sign out and sign in again with your password or Passport file.
passport.passwordChanged: Password changed. Other devices were signed out.
passport.createIntro: This account does not have a Passport yet. Create one to be able to export a recovery file and sign in on other MeshCrowd servers.
passport.created: Passport created. Export a backup file now.
passport.strengthenIntro: Right now this server receives your password every time you sign in, so whoever runs it could read it and open your Passport backup. After strengthening, your password is turned into two keys on your device: the server only gets a sign-in key and can no longer read your password or your backup. Choose a new password: this server has already seen the current one.
passport.strengthenAndroidWarning: Warning: after this, the current Android app can no longer sign in to this account with a password until it is updated. Signing in on the web and in the desktop app keeps working.
passport.strengthenMismatch: The new passwords do not match.
passport.strengthenSamePassword: The new password must be different from the current one.
passport.strengthened: Sign-in strengthened. Other devices were signed out.
passport.strengthenDone: Strengthened sign-in is on: this server never receives your password.
passport.restoreIntro: Choose your Passport file and its passphrase to bring your key back to this device. Enter your current password as well to make the server-side backup work again; this signs your other devices out.
passport.strengthenNeedsRestore: Strengthening sign-in needs your Passport key on this device, so restore it first.
passport.restorePasswordHint: Optional. Leave it empty to restore only on this device; the server backup then stays unreadable until your next password change.
passport.restoreWrongPassport: This Passport file belongs to a different account.
passport.restored: Passport restored and the server backup refreshed.
passport.restoredLocalOnly: Passport restored on this device. The server backup stays unreadable until your next password change.
passport.noKeyFileOption: I don't have my Passport key file
passport.dropBackupHeading: Change password without your key file
passport.dropBackupWarning: I understand this discards my encrypted Passport backup on the server. I will need to create a new Passport export afterward if I want one.

settings.title: Site settings
settings.originsHint: One https:// origin per line, for example https://cdn.jsdelivr.net. Scripts loaded from these origins run with full access to the page.
settings.originsWarn: Scripts loaded from another origin run inside MeshCrowd with the viewer's session and can read or change anything the page can. Only add hosts you fully trust, as specific hosts, never wildcards.

bots.hint: A bot is an account that answers when you @mention it or message it directly. It can think with an AI provider, be driven from outside through the bot API and a webhook, or both. Everything an AI bot is asked is sent to its AI provider.
bots.privacyNotice: Chats with this bot are sent to the AI provider "{provider}". Encrypted conversations and Notes channels are never read.
bots.personaPlaceholder: e.g. You are a friendly helper for our community. Keep answers short.
bots.mentionLabel: Answer when mentioned in channels and threads
bots.dmLabel: Allow private messages with this bot
bots.deleteMessage: Remove {name} from the server? Its old messages stay.
bots.noProviders: No AI provider is available. Ask a site admin to add one and allow server admins to use it.
bots.providersHint: Providers are the AI services bots talk to: Ollama on this machine, your LAN, a VPN or a VPS, or any OpenAI-compatible service. The API key is stored encrypted and never shown again.
bots.providerKeySet: A key is stored. Leave empty to keep it, type a new one to replace it.
bots.providerModels: Allowed models (one per line, empty = any)
bots.providerUsable: Server admins may use this provider
bots.apiHint: A bot token lets an outside tool read and post as this bot through /api/bot. It is shown only once.
bots.apiShownOnce: Copy it now, it will not be shown again.
bots.webhookHint: Signed JSON events are sent to this URL when someone mentions the bot or messages it. n8n, scripts and other tools can answer through the bot API.
bots.webhookScopeAll: Every message the bot can see
bots.webhookNoSecret: No secret yet. Generate one before enabling the webhook.
bots.webhookPrivate: Only a site admin can point a webhook at a private address.
bots.saveFirst: Save the bot first to set up API access and the webhook.

automod.title: AutoMod
automod.hint: Rules are checked before a message is posted. A message that breaks a rule is refused and logged, and the rule can also time the author out. The owner and anyone who can manage messages are never filtered, and a rule can exempt roles and channels.

onboarding.hint: Ask new members to read and accept the rules before they can take part, and let their answers to a few questions pick roles for them. Members who are already here are not affected. Until they accept, new members can read but not post, react or join voice.

reactionRoles.hint: Pick a message and an emoji: members who react with it get the role, and lose it again when they remove the reaction. The emoji is added to the message for you. Roles with moderation or management powers cannot be used here.

templates.title: Server templates
templates.hint: A template is a frozen copy of this server's structure: roles with their permissions, categories, channels and channel permissions. Anyone with the code can start a new server from it. Members, messages, emoji, bots and invites are never copied. Use Update after you change the server to refresh a template.
templates.name: Template name
templates.deleteMessage: The code stops working. Servers already made from it are not affected.
templates.codeHint: Start from a template: its roles, categories and channels are copied into your new server.

insights.title: Insights
insights.hint: Activity and growth of this server, read from the messages and memberships it already has. Times are UTC.
insights.footnote: Only plain messages written by people in channels and threads are counted: no DMs, bots, webhooks or system messages. Results refresh about once a minute.

ageGate.channelHint: Members have to confirm once that they are 18 or older before they can read or write here. It is a click-through only: nothing is verified.
ageGate.title: Age-restricted channel
ageGate.body: This channel may contain content meant for adults. Confirm that you are 18 or older to continue. You only have to do this once.

verification.label: Verification level
verification.hint: Holds back brand-new accounts and recent joiners from posting. The owner and anyone with a role are never held back. Nothing is checked outside this server.
verification.level1: Low - account at least 5 minutes old
verification.level2: Medium - account 5 minutes old and member for 10 minutes
verification.level3: High - account 7 days old and member for 10 minutes
